extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors and people who want to file a U.S. patent application without an attorney
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, step-by-step how-to guide for inventors who want to prepare, draft, and file patent applications at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office and handle prosecution, maintenance, and commercialization themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to patents and other intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of patents and other forms of intellectual property and guidance on when patent protection is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides foundational orientation for deciding whether and how to pursue patent protection (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: The science and magic of inventing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the inventive process itself — how inventions are conceived and developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practical considerations about inventing that affect patent strategy and preparation (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and the PPA
rubrics_metrics.description: How to document inventions properly and how to prepare and use a provisional patent application (PPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the role of documentation and the PPA in preserving priority and supporting later nonprovisional filings (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Will your invention sell?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of commercial viability and marketability as part of deciding whether to pursue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages evaluating potential market and business considerations before investing in patenting (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Is it patentable?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether an invention meets the legal requirements for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides readers through the substantive patentability inquiry (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and you may find
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting prior art searches to discover relevant publications and patents that affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instruction on how to search and interpret prior art to assess novelty and non-obviousness (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: What should I do next?
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision points and next steps after initial evaluation and searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps inventors choose among filing provisional/nonprovisional, refining the invention, or abandoning the effort (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to draft the specification and initial drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for drafting the patent specification and preparing required drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers content and form of the written description and drawings needed to support claims (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Now for the legalese : the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write patent claims — the legal definitions of the invention — including structure and scope considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance on claim drafting, claim scope, and claim language (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finaling and filing your application
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps and checklist for finalizing application documents and filing with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of the latest USPTO rules and forms to complete filing (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to market your invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for commercialization and marketing of an invention, independent of or alongside patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on business and marketing approaches to monetize inventions (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Going abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies and procedures for seeking patent protection outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers foreign filing options and timing considerations (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the PTO to deliver
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on prosecution before the USPTO, including responding to office actions and managing correspondence to advance an application to allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tactics for interacting with the PTO to move applications through examination (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Your application can have children
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of continuations, divisionals, and continuations-in-part to derive additional applications from an earlier filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains family practice and procedural options to expand or preserve claim scope (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: After your patent issues : use, maintenance, and infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant obligations and enforcement: maintenance fees, practicing the patent, and handling infringement issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers life-of-patent considerations including maintenance and enforcement strategies (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership, assignment, and licensing of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and practical rules about who owns inventions and how to assign or license patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on transfers of title, licensing deals, and related documentation (chapter listed in table of contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with latest USPTO rules and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and adherence to the most recent U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rules and forms when preparing and filing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The edition is 'Thoroughly updated to reflect the latest changes in intellectual property law' and 'provides the latest U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rules and forms.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing considerations under the America Invents Act (first-to-file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding how the America Invents Act's first-to-file framework affects filing strategy and priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 18th edition 'covers the latest implications of the first-to-file rules created by the America Invents Act,' indicating instruction on timing and priority strategy.
